observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2: a used inline 4-cylinder petrol engine sitting on a wet concrete floor among other engines, with hoses and wiring harness still attached.

Photos 0 and 1: front view of the timing cover with crank pulley, idler pulley, water pump pulley, another accessory pulley, an engine mount bracket and an alternator on the right; oil filter at the bottom.
Photo 2: top view of the cam cover shows four empty spark plug wells with no ignition coils fitted, an oil filler cap, a blue sticker and handwritten marks; intake manifold on the left.
Photos 0 and 1: a barcode label on the cylinder head reads only partly ('...A62' and '047'); no engine code such as a stamped block code is readable.
No maker's name or engine code is readable in any photo; the layout looks like a Toyota AZ family engine, but that is not read off the item.
Photos 0 and 1: orange cable or conduit is visible at the top right, which on some engines means a hybrid variant; it may belong to a neighbouring engine.
Engine is dirty with surface rust on brackets and bolts and oil stains; no photo shows the sides, the block stamp, the oil, or the engine running.
All photos carry a 'Posted on Jiji' watermark and a seller name.

identity.kind: complete 4-cylinder petrol car engine (Toyota AZ family by appearance, code unread)

claims.evidence: Photo 2 shows the four spark plug wells empty with no ignition coils; the starter and the other sides are not shown.

claims.claim: For Toyota vehicles like SUVs and crossovers, Toyota RAV4 second generation XA20
claims.evidence: No engine code or Toyota marking is readable; the block stamp is not shown.

risks.risk: Engine code unknown: a 2.0, a 2.4 or a hybrid variant of this family are priced very differently and fit different cars.
risks.proof: A close, sharp photo of the engine code and serial stamped on the block, with a handwritten code beside it.
risks.if_unproven: no price until the code is read

risks.risk: Engine may knock, burn oil, have low compression, stripped head bolt threads or a cracked block.
risks.proof: A clip with sound of the engine started on a test stand or in a car, idling and revving, plus a photo of the dipstick oil.

risks.risk: Ignition coils, sensors or the starter may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo of each side of the engine and of the coils and starter laid beside it.

risks.risk: Engine may be from a hybrid car, which does not swap into a normal car.
risks.proof: A photo of the block code plate and of the full engine with its orange cables traced or shown absent.

risks.risk: Engine may be stolen or its serial mismatched.
risks.proof: A photo of the serial stamp and the import or purchase document carrying the same serial.
risks.if_unproven: serial checked by the agent at collection before money moves

proof_requests: Close, sharp photo of the engine code and serial stamped on the block, with a handwritten code beside it.
Clip with sound of the engine running and revving on a test stand.
Photos of each side of the engine and the bottom, with coils and starter shown if included.
Photo of the dipstick oil and the coolant.
Import or purchase document carrying the same serial.
response.reason: The engine code is not readable in any photo and it sets the price, since a 2.0, a 2.4 and a hybrid variant of this layout differ widely; the 'complete' claim is also contradicted by the missing ignition coils in photo 2. A clear photo of the block stamp would allow a worst case price.
